question: In Figure 1B-2, if a proposed change is accepted for Federal rulemaking, what process follows before a Final Rule is published?
model_answer: Direct Answer: According to Figure 1B-2, once a proposed change is accepted for Federal rulemaking, FHWA develops the device provisions for inclusion in the next Notice of Proposed Amendments, publishes that Notice in the Federal Register, holds a docket comment period, reviews the comments received, and then prepares the Final Rule before publishing it. In parallel, the change may also be considered for interim approval, allowing optional use of the device pending completion of the rulemaking. After the Final Rule is published, State manuals must be brought into substantial conformance within 2 years. Standards (mandatory): - "States or other Federal agencies that have their own MUTCDs or Supplements shall revise these MUTCDs or Supplements to be in substantial conformance with changes to the National MUTCD within 2 years of the effective date of the Final Rule for the changes [23 CFR 655.603(b)(3)]." Options (permitted): - Interim approval may run in parallel with rulemaking: "Interim approval allows for the optional use of a traffic control device or application and does not create a new mandate or recommendation for its use," with jurisdictions agreeing to conditions "until an official rulemaking action has occurred." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 1B-2 shows the "YES" branch from "Accepted for Federal rulemaking?" flowing through: FHWA develops device provisions for inclusion in the next Notice of Proposed Amendments → FHWA publishes Notice of Proposed Amendments in Federal Register → Docket comment period → FHWA reviews comments → FHWA prepares Final Rule → FHWA publishes Final Rule, with a parallel "Interim approval?" decision leading to interim approval issuance and deployment. [Image 3] Page 11 explains that a device under interim approval might be proposed for adoption in the next scheduled rulemaking, and if not, its status will be stated in the Federal Register notice. [Image 4] Page 9 states that the process for incorporating new traffic control devices into the Manual is shown in Figure 1B-2. Citations: - Figure 1B-2 (p.9) - Section 1B.07 Support §3 (p.11) - Section 1B.07 Support §4 (p.11) - Section 1B.06 Support §4 (p.9) - Section 1B.02 Standard §2 (p.4)
gold_answer: FHWA develops provisions for a Notice of Proposed Amendments, publishes the notice in the Federal Register, holds a docket comment period, reviews comments, prepares the Final Rule, and publishes it.
